test: melt with real routing fees on regtest (#1103)

* test: melt with real routing fees on regtest

Add melt tests that pay invoices from nodes the mint has no direct channel to, so payments route through lnd-1 and incur a real routing fee. The routed destination differs per backend: lnd-2 for LND-backed mints, cln-1 for CLN-backed. The invoice helper waits for gossip to propagate first, since CLN nodes take up to a minute after boot to learn non-adjacent nodes. Existing zero-fee tests are unchanged.

* chore: conform fee tests

Replace the callable-based gossip wait with a command-and-key helper, drop the multi-line docstrings and wrapped comments, and use the existing .copy()/.extend() idiom and SLEEP_TIME constant. Assertion messages now match the short Title-case style used elsewhere in the suite. No behavior change.

* test: melt with real routing fees on regtest

Add melt tests that pay invoices from nodes the mint has no direct
channel to, so payments route through lnd-1 and incur a real routing
fee. The routed destination differs per backend: lnd-2 for LND-backed
mints, cln-1 for CLN-backed. A 1000 sat melt costs 1001 msat, which
also covers the mint rounding sub-sat fees up to the next sat. The
invoice helper waits for gossip to propagate first, since CLN nodes
take up to a minute after boot to learn non-adjacent nodes. Existing
zero-fee tests are unchanged.

* chore: assert melt response in routed fee test

The wallet-level routed melt test now also checks the melt response state and payment preimage instead of only the balance, matching what the mint-level test asserts.

* chore: tighten routed-fee melt test assertions

Assert fee bounds on the db-persisted fee_paid instead of a value derived
from the change, so the fee-reserve limit check can actually fail, and
verify the change compensates exactly for the unspent reserve. Drop a
tautological balance assert from the wallet-side test, which has no
independent fee signal to bound against.

* chore: deflake routed-fee tests in ci

Wait until the mint's node can compute a route (queryroutes/getroute)
instead of only seeing the destination's node announcement, which races
channel-policy gossip on fresh CI environments and caused NO_ROUTE
failures. Skip the exact fee-rounding test on CLN backends, whose
randomized pathfinding may pick a costlier route than the assertion
assumes.

even though `lock p2pk` already prints --timelock guidance for the
`send` command it tells users to run, which had no such flag. Thread
an optional per-send override through helpers.send() into both the
P2PK and P2BK lock paths (same mechanism, same code shape); omitting
the flag preserves the existing settings fallback exactly. Also fixes
lock_p2pk's printed send command to include --timelock when set.

fix(wallet): derive mint_wallet db location from receiver wallet on receive paths

receive_cli and redeem_TokenV3 constructed the throwaway mint_wallet's db
directory by re-deriving os.path.join(settings.cashu_dir, wallet.name)
instead of reusing the receiving wallet's actual wallet.db.db_location.

For CLI-constructed wallets this is a no-op: the CLI always builds wallets
with db_path = os.path.join(settings.cashu_dir, walletname), so the two
expressions are identical. But for wallets created with a custom db
directory (library/test usage), re-deriving the path from cashu_dir + name
can point at a different on-disk wallet than the one actually receiving,
reintroducing the same key-mismatch/missing-witness failure that the
previous commit (94d7eca) fixed for non-default wallet names.

Use wallet.db.db_location at both call sites instead, aligning them with
the balance, pending, and init_auth_wallet call sites, which already
reconstruct wallets from wallet.db.db_location. Addresses PR review
feedback from Copilot noting the directory argument was still re-derived
even after the name argument was fixed.

Also drops the now-unused `import os` in cashu/wallet/helpers.py, and adds
a regression test pinning that redeem_TokenV3 uses the receiver's real db
location rather than settings.cashu_dir + name.

test(wallet): add regression tests for named-wallet P2PK receive

Covers the receive_TokenV3/receive_cli path directly: (a) a plain
P2PK-locked token received into a non-default-named wallet succeeds
end-to-end, and (b) the mint_wallet constructed inside redeem_TokenV3
shares the receiving wallet's private key rather than a fresh one.
Verified both fail with "Witness is missing for p2pk signature" against
the pre-fix code and pass against the fix.

fix(wallet): pass wallet name when constructing mint_wallet on receive paths

Wallet.with_db derives the sqlite filename from its name kwarg (default
"wallet") while the directory is passed separately. receive_cli and
redeem_TokenV3 passed the directory but omitted name=, so the throwaway
mint_wallet opened <cashu_dir>/<walletname>/wallet.sqlite3 instead of
<cashu_dir>/<walletname>/<walletname>.sqlite3 whenever walletname !=
"wallet". The mismatched (empty) DB caused a fresh mnemonic to be
generated, so the receiving wallet's key didn't match the lock and
locked proofs were submitted with witness=None, rejected by the mint.

fix(mint): commit PENDING before async melt response (#1087)

async_melt used to return PENDING while still leaving the quote and proofs
UNPAID until a detached melt() task interacted with them. That window made
NUT-17/polls see UNPAID (treated as payment failure) while the mint went on
to spend the proofs.

Split melt into _prepare_melt (validate, lock quote+proofs PENDING, store
blank outputs) and _execute_melt_payment (settle/pay/finalize with the
existing rollback paths). async_melt now prepares, returns the durable
PENDING state, then runs only payment in the background.

fix(test): align test_generate_change_promises_zero_fee_deletes_all_blanks with fix

The test was added in 9fed0f0 (PR #795) with a name asserting deletion
("..._deletes_all_blanks") but assertions baked in the then-current bug
where the overpaid_fee <= 0 early-return skipped cleanup. This PR
completes the fix; flip the assertions to match the fixed behavior the
test name already claimed.

Also apply KvngMikey's review suggestion: guard the cleanup with
`outputs is not None` so we don't issue a no-op DELETE when the wallet
sent no blanks to begin with.

refactor(test): collapse melt early-return tests via parametrize

The two `overpaid_fee == 0` / `overpaid_fee < 0` cases differ only in
one integer offset, so collapse them into a single parametrized test
and drop the `_run_melt_with_patched_fee` helper / `INVOICE_64_SAT`
module constant — the invoice is inlined to match the style of the
other tests in this file.

fix(mint): clean up blank outputs on melt change early-return

`_generate_change_promises` already deletes the wallet's blank NUT-08
outputs from `promises` after signing them. But when the function takes
the early-return branch (overpaid_fee <= 0 or no outputs supplied) those
rows were left behind with `c_ IS NULL` — and later operations that
re-derive the same `B_` (notably NUT-13 seed restore) collide with them
and surface as `OutputsArePendingError`.

Also soften the negative-overpaid_fee log to debug with a message that
explains the case: in practice the backend can report a fee greater
than the wallet-provided reserve (e.g. an LNbits backend skimming a
service fee on top of the routing fee), so an error-level log here is
noisy and misleading.

Adds two regression tests covering both the `overpaid_fee == 0` and
`overpaid_fee < 0` branches.

m019_add_p2pk_e_to_proofs adds the column to both proofs and

p2pk_e survived (fails against the pre-fix code).

test(p2bk): import official NUT-28 test vectors

Reimplementation-style tests can share a systematic misreading of the
spec with the implementation; canonical vectors are the cross-
implementation fixed point cdk and cashu-ts already grade themselves
against. Adds tests/nuts/test_nut28_test_vectors.py, verifying
derive_blinding_scalar, blind_pubkeys, and derive_blinded_private_key
byte-exact against cashubtc/nuts tests/28-tests.md across all 11 defined slots.
All vectors pass.

fix(p2bk): replace bare-except HTLC slot skip with explicit SecretKind check

_derive_p2bk_signing_keys() wrapped derive_blinded_private_key() in a bare
except Exception to skip the HTLC hashlock at slot 0, which also silently
swallowed genuine derivation errors (e.g. a corrupted p2pk_e) at any slot.
Per NUT-28's kind-agnostic slot numbering ([data, ...pubkeys, ...refund]),
branch on SecretKind instead: HTLC secrets skip slot 0 deterministically
since data is a preimage hash, not a pubkey; pubkeys/refund still start at
slot 1. Any exception from derive_blinded_private_key() now propagates.

Tests: rebuild the HTLC+P2BK secret via natural slot-1 construction
instead of a throwaway slot-0 pubkey, add a refund-slot-offset case, and
add a regression test proving a corrupted p2pk_e now raises instead of
being silently swallowed (fails against the pre-fix code).

* feat(crypto): deterministic DLEQ nonce derivation (NUT-12)

Derive the DLEQ nonce `r` deterministically from the private key and
proof context instead of from the RNG:

  r = HMAC-SHA256(key=a, "Cashu_DLEQ_R_v1" || A || B' || C' || ctr) mod n

This removes the dependency on RNG quality. Reusing `r` across two
proofs with different challenges would leak the private key.

`step2_bob` now emits deterministic nonces for every signature; DLEQ
verification is unaffected since (e, s) remain valid proofs. The
`p_bytes` override is retained for the existing test vectors.

Adds the NUT-12 deterministic-nonce test vector (cashubtc/nuts#368)
plus reproducibility and context-sensitivity tests.

fix(lightning): return UNKNOWN (not FAILED) on ambiguous LND pay errors

A transport/RPC error or a mid-stream gateway error does not tell us
whether the payment was attempted or is in flight. Returning FAILED in
those cases asserts a failure we cannot prove. Report UNKNOWN instead so
the ledger re-checks the real state via TrackPaymentV2; FAILED is now
returned only when LND explicitly rejects the request pre-initiation or
reports a terminal Payment.status == FAILED.

  pre-initiation rejection stays FAILED)

fix(lightning): migrate LND backends to SendPaymentV2 for lnd 0.21 compatibility

lnd v0.21.0-beta removed the deprecated lnrpc.SendPaymentSync RPC and its
REST route POST /v1/channels/transactions, which both LND backends used to
pay invoices. Every melt against an lnd 0.21 node fails immediately with
{"code":5,"message":"Not Found"} from the REST proxy (or the gRPC
equivalent) before any payment attempt is made.

Migrate pay_invoice in lndrest and lnd_grpc to the streaming
routerrpc.SendPaymentV2 (POST /v2/router/send), consuming updates until a
terminal payment status is reached, mirroring the TrackPaymentV2 handling
already used by get_payment_status. Invoice creation, status checks and the
MPP path (SendToRouteV2) were already on non-removed endpoints.

fix(mint): enforce unique x-coordinates in p2pk pubkey deduplication (#969)

Deduplication logic for p2pk pubkeys was previously based solely on the exact lowercase hex string.
Since Schnorr signatures verify against the x-only representation, a single pubkey could be
supplied in multiple differently compressed forms (e.g., '02' and '03' prefixes) and incorrectly
pass the uniqueness check.

This commit updates the deduplication check in LedgerSpendingConditions to strip SEC-1 prefixes
and enforce uniqueness based on the public key's 32-byte x-coordinate, along with a test
that verifies this behavior.

fix: use -- before quote ID in management CLI tests (#912)

Quote IDs are base64url strings (e.g. -JmECgu3Hxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx).
When a quote ID starts with '-', Click treats it as a CLI option and exits
with usage error (SystemExit 2).

Add -- before quote_id in runner.invoke() so everything after is parsed
as positional arguments. This applies to update mint-quote, update melt-quote,
get mint-quote, and get melt-quote commands.

feat: proxy-aware rate limiting with sane defaults

Enable rate limiting by default (mint_rate_limit=True) and add
proxy-aware client IP resolution for mints behind reverse proxies
(Caddy, nginx) or CDNs (Cloudflare).

New settings:
- MINT_RATE_LIMIT_PROXY_TRUST (default: True) - extract client IP
  from proxy headers (CF-Connecting-IP, X-Forwarded-For) instead of
  using the direct connection IP. Disable if the mint is directly
  exposed to the internet.
- MINT_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (default: "127.0.0.1") - which proxy IPs
  uvicorn trusts for X-Forwarded-For. Set to "*" if your proxy's IP
  is dynamic.

Default rate limits (unchanged):
- Global: 60 requests/minute per IP
- Transaction endpoints: 20 requests/minute per IP

fix: correct inverted expiry check in mint quote validation (#858)

The expiry check was using > instead of <, which caused the mint to reject
valid quotes (expiry in the future) and accept expired quotes (expiry in
the past).

quote.expiry is a Unix timestamp representing when the quote expires.
The previous check `quote.expiry > int(time.time())` would evaluate to True
for valid quotes where expiry is in the future, incorrectly raising
"quote expired".

Changed to `quote.expiry < int(time.time())` which correctly identifies
expired quotes where the expiry timestamp is in the past.
